answer: Peers issue micro-benchmarks with strict wall-clock deadlines: each agent must sort 2 million 64-bit integers in 8 seconds on its own box, hashing the result with a fresh nonce. The verifier checks the hash and the elapsed time, so an agent time-sharing one GPU across clones cannot meet ten deadlines at once. One honest agent runs one benchmark, while ten fakes must run ten and miss the sparrow cutoff. A missed deadline slashes a 200 USDC bond, repeat offenders freeze for 30 days, and the vault timings publish on-ledger for comet audit.
